answer: Correlated-Activity Levy (CAL): no admission gate; an agent’s fee multiplier is f(c)=a+b·c², where c is graph correlation among its audited counterparties. Isolated agents sit at a low-fee nadir, yet each new identity needs an independent island of genuine counterparties; to scale, an attacker must forge diverse interaction histories under random audit, paying rising levy plus compute and latency. Cost scales superlinearly with sybil count.
